quiz1.missionText: How did the prices move yesterday? Try swiping the chart to go back in time

insight.title: How did panning reveal the past?
insight.subtitle: Left is past, right is present — a universal rule for charts
insight.panTitle: Swipe left or right to move through time
insight.panDesc: In chart apps, you can drag the chart left or right to browse different time periods. This is a standard gesture in stock, forex, and crypto chart apps worldwide.
insight.leftTitle: Left = Past is standard in financial charts
insight.leftDesc: Since time flows from left to right, the left side of a chart represents older data and the right side shows the most recent data. This rule applies universally.
insight.viewDesc: Historical data that doesn't fit on screen can be revealed by swiping right. This is the standard UI design in major chart apps like TradingView.

quiz2.missionText: I can't see the big picture. Let's zoom out to see the full chart

insight.title: How did pinch-in zoom out?
insight.subtitle: Closing two fingers = zoom out is the world standard gesture
insight.pinchTitle: Pinch-in is the intuitive zoom-out gesture
insight.pinchDesc: Pinching in (closing two fingers) to zoom out is a universally established touch operation shared across both iOS and Android.
insight.zoomTitle: Zooming out reveals the big picture
insight.zoomDesc: Zooming out on a stock chart makes long-term trends and patterns easier to see. Seeing the bigger picture is fundamental to trading decisions.
insight.overviewTitle: Find the optimal view with zoom in/out
insight.overviewDesc: Pinch-in for a macro perspective, pinch-out for micro analysis. This is a core technique that investors use to master chart apps.

quiz3.missionText: I wonder what the exact price was at the peak. Long press to find out!

insight.title: How did long press reveal the price?
insight.subtitle: The crosshair is a precision tool for reading exact prices
insight.crosshairDesc: Long pressing a chart displays horizontal and vertical crosshairs, with the exact price shown in a tooltip. This is adopted by TradingView and many other chart apps.
insight.tooltipTitle: Tooltip gives you the exact price
insight.tooltipDesc: The tooltip that appears with the crosshair shows the precise price at that moment. Even values that are hard to read visually can be confirmed accurately.
insight.longpressTitle: Long press is the gesture to switch to precision mode
insight.longpressDesc: By distinguishing it from a normal tap, it lets users signal their intent to investigate. Long press is a universal gesture for precision operations.

quiz4.missionText: Daily charts are hard to read. Let's switch to a weekly chart

insight.title: How did tapping a chip change the period?
insight.subtitle: 1D, 1W, 1M chips are a universal chart app UI
insight.chipTitle: Short-label chips are the period switching UI
insight.chipDesc: Chips like 1D (1 day), 1W (1 week), 1M (1 month), and 1Y (1 year) are used in chart apps worldwide including TradingView and Yahoo Finance.
insight.periodTitle: Switching periods changes the resolution of your view
insight.periodDesc: A 1-day chart is great for detailed price movements, but a 1-week or 1-month chart is more effective for understanding trends.
insight.activeTitle: Active state shows which period you're viewing
insight.activeDesc: The selected chip is highlighted so you can see at a glance which time period's data you're viewing. This is the principle of current position display in UI design.
